headline: Equities enter a pivotal earnings and inflation week near all-time highs, with Strait of Hormuz tensions keeping oil and yields elevated above comfort zones.
stance: Constructive but on alert. The S&P 500 closed Friday only ~45 points below its June all-time high of 7,620, supported by broadening breadth and a strong AI/tech bid — yet the 10-year yield (prior close 4.56%) is at its highest since late May, real rates sit at 2.32%, and the equity risk premium has turned negative (-2.05%), meaning bonds are effectively competing with stocks for the first time in this cycle. This week is binary: Tuesday's June CPI (expected -0.1% month-over-month headline) and the same-day big-bank earnings deluge (JPM, BAC, GS, WFC, C) will either confirm the soft-landing story or rattle it — and Fed Chair Warsh testifies to Congress the same day.

news.head: Strait of Hormuz — shipping risk lingers
news.body: U.S.-Iran strikes earlier in the week rocked the Strait of Hormuz and shipping has slowed considerably; a ceasefire remains tenuous, though neither side has confirmed a waterway closure, keeping oil choppy rather than spiking.

news.head: SK Hynix debut — record IPO lifts chip sentiment
news.body: South Korean memory giant SK Hynix raised $26.5 billion in the largest-ever U.S. listing by a foreign company, with its ADRs (SKHYV) opening at $170 — roughly 14% above the $149 offer price — providing a positive signal for the AI chip complex heading into TSM and ASML earnings this week.

news.head: Meta +15% on the week — AI cost structure surprise
news.body: Meta surged about 6% on Friday alone after a SemiAnalysis report on its AI compute business went viral, capping a ~15% weekly gain — its best weekly performance since early 2024 — driven by reporting suggesting Meta may be dramatically improving its AI cost structure and targeting 14GW of compute capacity in 2026–27.

news.head: Delta beats but stock slides
news.body: Delta Air Lines beat second-quarter top- and bottom-line estimates but fell roughly 1.7% on Friday as investors focused on cautious forward guidance in an environment of elevated fuel costs tied to Hormuz uncertainty.

news.head: Fed holds at 3.50–3.75%, drops easing bias
news.body: The FOMC's June minutes confirmed a unanimous decision to hold rates at 3.50–3.75% and removed language implying an easing bias, with the committee noting the S&P 500 climbed nearly 6% over the inter-meeting period and flagging lingering inflation risk.

news.head: Margin debt hits record — speculative excess signal
news.body: Debit balances in brokerage margin accounts hit a record $1.42 trillion in May, up 53.7% year-over-year, a sign of elevated leverage in the system as markets approach all-time highs.

news.head: Warsh testifies Tuesday — first Capitol Hill appearance
news.body: Fed Chair Kevin Warsh makes his first trip to the House Financial Services Committee on Tuesday July 14, coinciding with CPI and big-bank earnings — a rare triple-catalyst morning.

implications: The negative equity risk premium (-2.05%) means the stock market is offering less expected return than risk-free Treasuries — a structural headwind if yields stay elevated.
A hot CPI on Tuesday could push the 10-year yield (prior close 4.56%, already at a 7-week high) toward the May peak near 4.67%, compressing multiples on a CAPE of 42.18 that has no cushion.
A soft CPI (-0.1% MoM as expected) paired with solid bank earnings could be the catalyst for a break above the June all-time high of 7,620 on the S&P 500.
Oil (prior close $71.51/bbl WTI) rose 4% on the week on Hormuz fears — sustained pressure above $75 would re-open the door to an emergency Fed discussion, even with the current hold.

The yen (prior close 161.67 ¥/$) is at a 3-year extreme (98.5th percentile) — Japan's push to steer pension funds toward domestic assets introduces a tail risk of rapid yen strengthening and pressure on U.S. Treasuries held by Japanese investors.

Positioning: Speculators have almost no bullish bets left in Russell 2000 futures (2nd percentile of 3 years) — a contrarian floor for small-caps. Similarly, specs are extended short British Pound (2nd percentile) and 3M SOFR (2nd percentile), both contrarian-bullish signals. On the other side, speculators are heavily positioned long Copper (94th percentile of 3 years) — a contrarian warning for industrial metals. WTI Crude spec longs sit at the 10th percentile — not yet a extended long despite the week's oil spike.

watch.head: Tue 8:30am ET — June CPI
watch.body: Consensus expects headline CPI -0.1% month-over-month and core +0.3% MoM / +2.9% YoY; a surprise to the upside could push the 10-year yield above 4.60% and pressure equity valuations sharply.

watch.head: Tue pre-market — Big Bank earnings
watch.body: JPMorgan, Bank of America, Goldman Sachs, Wells Fargo, and Citigroup all report Tuesday morning — the earliest and broadest read on credit quality, loan demand, and net interest margin in this rate environment.

watch.head: Tue — Warsh congressional testimony
watch.body: Fed Chair Warsh's first Capitol Hill appearance will be parsed word-by-word for any shift in the Fed's rate trajectory after June's removal of the easing bias.

watch.head: Wed — ASML Q2 earnings
watch.body: ASML's order book is the clearest leading indicator of global semiconductor capex; any guidance cut would hit the entire chip complex and likely weigh on TSM (reports Thu) and the broader Nasdaq.

watch.head: Thu — TSM Q2 earnings
watch.body: Taiwan Semiconductor reports Thursday; after a 35% revenue surge year-over-year in Q1, investors need confirmation that AI-driven wafer demand is sustaining — a key catalyst for the Nasdaq setup.

watch.head: Hormuz weekend headlines
watch.body: Any escalation or progress in Qatar-mediated U.S.-Iran diplomacy over the weekend could gap oil and safe-haven assets sharply at Monday's open; monitor Sunday evening futures.

watch.head: USD/JPY at extreme (161.67 ¥/$)
watch.body: Japan's pension-fund domestic-reallocation signal is a policy-driven yen catalyst — a sharp yen rally from these extremes would force unwind of yen-funded carry trades and could create sudden volatility in global equities.

sections.title: Macro & Rates
bullets: 10-year Treasury yield: 4.56% (prior Fri close) — up 9 basis points on the week, the highest level since late May, driven by Hormuz-related oil/inflation fears and the Fed's hawkish June minutes.
2-year yield: 4.21% (prior Fri close); the yield curve (2s10s) is +35 basis points — gently positive, consistent with a no-recession, higher-for-longer pricing.
Real (inflation-adjusted) 10-year rate: 2.32% — meaningfully restrictive and the primary gravitational force on high-multiple growth stocks.

10-year breakeven inflation: 2.24% (prior Fri close) — markets are not pricing a runaway inflation scenario yet, but one-year household inflation expectations ticked up to 3.7% in June, the highest since September 2023.
Fed funds rate held at 3.50–3.75% (unanimous June vote); real fed funds rate is only +0.21% — still below neutral, limiting how restrictive policy actually is.
Financial conditions remain easy: the Chicago Fed's ANFCI reads -0.506 and the St. Louis FSI reads -0.72, both signaling looser-than-normal conditions despite elevated yields.
Bond market volatility (MOVE index: 69.5) is subdued — the Treasury market is not flashing a systemic stress signal ahead of CPI week.
Term premium on 10-year Treasuries: 73 basis points — investors are demanding meaningfully more compensation for holding long bonds, a structural headwind for duration.
sections.positioning: Speculators have almost no bullish bets left in 3M SOFR futures (2nd percentile of 3 years, a 3-year low) — a contrarian-bullish lean for short-end rates, suggesting the market may be over-positioned for rate hikes that don't materialize.

sections.title: Equity Markets
bullets: S&P 500: 7,575.39 (prior Fri close, +0.42% on the day) — roughly 45 points below the June all-time high of 7,620; Nasdaq Composite: 26,281.61 (prior Fri close, +0.29%); Dow: 52,637.01 (prior Fri close, +0.29%).

Nasdaq 100 futures overnight: ~30,032 (pre-market level) — well above the prior Fri NDX cash close of 26,281 on the Composite, with the NDX index itself last at 26,281.61; note NQ futures at ~30,032 reflect the separate futures contract level.
Breadth is healthy: 65.8% of S&P 500 stocks trade above their 50-day moving average and 68.1% above their 200-day — not a narrow, mega-cap-only rally.
VIX: 15.03 (prior Fri close) — complacency territory; the market is not paying up for near-term protection even with CPI and bank earnings in two days.

SKEW index: 144.3 (prior Fri close) — elevated, meaning options traders are paying a significant premium for tail-risk hedges (deep out-of-the-money puts) even as VIX is calm — a split signal worth noting.
Nasdaq volatility (VXN): 24.89 (prior Fri close) — higher than VIX, reflecting residual chip-stock uncertainty ahead of ASML and TSM reports.
Meta +15% on the week was the standout; Nvidia +4% on Friday; chip stocks generally choppy — sector leadership is narrowing back toward mega-cap AI names after last week's broad rotation.
CAPE (Shiller P/E): 42.18 — historically stretched; leaves little room for an earnings or rate disappointment.
ISM Manufacturing: 53.3 (above 50 = expanding); ISM Services: 54.5 — both in expansion, supporting the soft-landing case but also arguing the Fed need not rush to cut.
sections.positioning: Speculators have almost no bullish bets left in Russell 2000 futures (2nd percentile of 3 years, spec net position at just 2.7% of open interest) — a contrarian floor for small-caps; any positive surprise from CPI or bank earnings could ignite a sharp squeeze higher in small-caps.

single_name.note: CarMax (Consumer Cyclical) — large off-exchange block buying (quiet institutional accumulation) and a burst of unusual options buying both active; company insiders have been buying (2 insider rules fired); 4.37 days-to-cover means shorts are moderately heavy with squeeze risk; trading above its 200-day moving average. Freshest signal in the consumer cyclical setup list.

sections.title: Credit & Liquidity
bullets: High-yield credit spread over investment-grade: 270 bps (prior reading) — not distressed, but wider than early-year lows; the HY/IG ETF ratio (1.3481) confirms risk appetite is intact but not euphoric.
Investment-grade option-adjusted spread: 76 bps — tight, consistent with low default expectations; credit is not warning of an equity selloff.
Commercial paper funding spread (CPFF): 18 bps — very low; short-term corporate funding is cheap and accessible, a green light for liquidity.
FRA-OIS and SOFR-OIS spreads: both -9 bps — negative readings indicate interbank funding is exceptionally smooth with no stress.
Bank credit growth: +5.93% year-over-year (as of July 1) — solid loan demand; SLOOS surveys show lending standards are barely tightening (C&I: 8.1%, CRE: 2.0%).

Fed reverse repo (RRP): $0.5 billion — essentially zero; excess liquidity has fully drained from the RRP facility, meaning any future liquidity squeeze comes directly from bank reserves ($3,098.9 billion), which remain ample.

Treasury General Account (TGA): $774.1 billion — a large government cash balance; if the Treasury draws it down to fund spending, that injects cash into the banking system and is a net liquidity positive for markets.
M2 money supply: +5.58% year-over-year — growing faster than nominal GDP trend, a mild tailwind for asset prices and a mild upside risk for inflation.

single_name.note: Scorpio Tankers (Energy/Shipping) — large off-exchange block buying active and a burst of unusual options buying detected; company insiders have been buying (2 insider rules fired); 4.0 days-to-cover means shorts are moderate with squeeze risk; trading above its 200-day moving average. Direct Hormuz/oil-supply-disruption beneficiary if tanker rerouting accelerates. Signal aging at 88% weight.
